Jane — thanks for the clear list. Drafting a concise reply and a pair of pragmatic architectures below; attaching a diagram that maps data flows and trust boundaries.

Recommendation summary (short):
- Preferred: Hybrid BYOK with customer-controlled master keys in an HSM (customer or co-located) + Redwood-managed envelope keys. This balances customer control with low-latency ops.
- Alternative: Fully customer-hosted HSM with Redwood integration over dedicated private link (we'll need cross-account PKCS#11 or a proxy). Strongest control, more ops burden.

Architecture A — Hybrid BYOK (recommended):
- Customer generates and stores a master (root) key in their HSM (PKCS#11 or Cloud HSM).
- Redwood maintains per-tenant envelope keys; all data keys are wrapped by the customer's master key before being persisted.
- Key rotation: Customer rotates master key at their cadence; Redwood rotates envelope keys (e.g., 90d) and rewraps under current master key via a rewrap window.
- Auditability: Redwood streams signed KMS operations to customer SIEM (TLS syslog) and provides immutable usage records.

Pros: customer retains ultimate key control, minimal performance impact for inference.
Cons: requires a short maintenance window for rewraps and a secure channel for PKCS#11/REST interactions.

Architecture B — Customer-hosted HSM (strong custody):
- All encryption/decryption operations requiring the master happen inside customer HSM. Redwood requests cryptographic operations via a dedicated private link.
- Redwood keeps only ephemeral cache (no long-term unwrapped keys).

Pros: strongest separation; meets strict regulator requirements.
Cons: higher latencies, availability dependency on customer infra, increased SLO coordination.

Operational notes / items we need from Acme:
- HSM model / vendor (if you have a preference) and attestation reports (FIPS level).
- Desired rotation cadence for master keys and any blackout windows.
- Whether your auditors need live access to audit logs or batch exports.

I've attached "encryption-arch-diagram.v1.pdf" showing the two flows and the proposed rewrap process. Proposed agenda for the design review:
  1) Walk through architectures (15m)
  2) Discuss key ceremony and procurement (10m)
  3) Rotation/Revocation runbooks (10m)
  4) Auditing and SIEM integration (10m)

If that looks good, I'll lock in Tue May 11 15:00 ET.

On 2026-05-09 11:05, Irene Choi wrote:
> Drafted two architectures — hybrid BYOK (recommended) and customer-hosted HSM.

Adding a product/ops perspective below. We'll be sensitive to latency and supportability — two things to call out:

1) Latency: if we do a remote HSM for every decryption, P50/P95 tokenization latency will increase. For hybrid BYOK we keep unwrapped envelope keys cached in a hardened key cache (TLS + mTLS) inside the VPC to avoid per-request HSM trips. Cache TTL and rewrap windows should be defined.

2) Rotation & rewrap policy: propose Redwood defaults: envelope key rotation every 90 days, replay-safe metadata, and a rewrap window (24–48 hrs) where the rewrap job runs at low traffic hours. We need to define an API for rewrap status and a safe rollback.

3) Emergency rotation: must include an automated path (API + human approval) and a manual key-ceremony fallback in case the automated channel breaks. This is where an offline key escrow or split knowledge (Shamir) backup can be valuable.

4) HSM compatibility: we support PKCS#11 and cloud HSM APIs (AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM). For on-prem appliances we'll need the model list and endpoint topology (load balancer, bastion). Require FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestation for on-prem HSMs.

Operational impact: we'll need one small feature to expose rewrap operations in the Redwood Console and to enable customer-provided attestation artifacts in the tenant Settings panel. I'll add a quick RFC for a minimal UI change.

Karthik
Head of Product | Redwood Inference

Jane / team — thanks for confirming the meeting. Quick follow-up and proposed next steps so we have a clear checklist post-call: 

Decisions (proposed, will confirm on the call):
- Go-forward: Hybrid BYOK with customer-controlled master key in Acme HSM + Redwood-managed envelope keys (we'll call this "Custodial Envelope Model").

Immediate action items (owners):
1) Acme: provide HSM vendor/model + current attestation packs (Jane) — due 2026-05-13.
2) Redwood Security (Irene): draft Key Policy & Rotation Playbook (will include an offline key ceremony appendix) — initial draft by 2026-05-14.
3) Redwood Ops (Evelyn): prepare rewrap job runbook and low-traffic rewrap window; include API endpoints for status — draft by 2026-05-15.
4) Both: SIEM integration test plan for signed rotation events (mutual TLS + syslog) — owners: Acme infra + Redwood platform — target test 2026-05-20.

Operational commitments & notes:
- Redwood confirms we will never persist customer master keys in plaintext. Master key operations will be proxied where required and only short-lived symmetric data keys will be cached inside the VPC.
- We will provide signed rotation events with timestamps and a unique operation id; logs will be signed with our KMS signing key and pushable to your SIEM.
- Emergency procedures: we will create an emergency key revocation runbook and a manual key-ceremony checklist; we recommend a split-knowledge escrow for offline backups.

Links / references:
- Design doc (internal): https://redwood.example.com/confluence/private-deployments/kms-hsm-design
